title: Stale asynchronous completion mutates a replacement UI context

scenario.observed_change: A UI mount awaits asynchronous data while navigation can replace the root. Completion of the old mount then looks up and mutates the current root instead of the root associated with the initiating operation.
controlled_inputs: timing of the first asynchronous load
navigation that replaces the mounted root before completion
authority_boundaries: state validated for the initiating mount versus state current at completion
old asynchronous operation versus replacement consumer context
operation_model: start mount A and begin asynchronous load
navigate away and mount replacement B
allow A to complete after B is current
stale continuation mutates or hides B

required_invariants.requirement: State or identity validated for an operation must remain bound to the effective target through use.
Lifecycle and asynchronous changes must cover materially reachable stale/current transition cases that share the same invariant.

must_investigate: whether an awaited continuation captures the initiating root or generation
whether success and failure completion can run after a replacement context becomes current
must_identify: the stale continuation can mutate the replacement consumer context
must_not_claim: safe remount behavior based only on direct-load or completed-navigation tests
that checking the current root after await preserves initiating-operation ownership

provenance.note: Codex identified that an older Playground mount could complete after instant navigation and hide the replacement root because the continuation did not preserve initiating root/generation identity.
